related_resources.reason: Examines changing lake shorelines, visibility, settlement and the temptation to treat the contact-period Pátzcuaro landscape as timeless.
Neutron activation analysis of pottery from four basin sites finds eight compositional groups, local recipes persisting through imperial formation and complex participation.
Combines soils, lake fluctuations and settlement estimates; cautions against treating ancient intensification as inevitably environmentally destructive.
Analyzes friar, Indigenous elites and native artists who shaped a mid-sixteenth-century source; narratives and images reveal colonial power negotiations, not neutral eyewitness to earlier centuries.
Identifies Tzintzuntzan as late Purépecha political/ceremonial center with yácatas, terraces and dynastic residences.
Discusses copper working, hammered and cast metals, workshops and supply from Tierra Caliente; broad museum interpretation rather than quantitative ore provenance study.
